_comment: Two tiles, cut where the partitioner cut. The ranges are derived from the partition JSON's contiguous hardware_target runs rather than transcribed, so a re-slice upstream moves them here too. The cut is load-bearing: the head's Resize/Slice/Softmax reject on HTA, so a single whole-network tile would pin the whole detector to one backend. Sub-DLCs come from slice_to_subonnx.py + build_subdlcs.sh.
_id_space_note: The IR this manifest indexes (yolov8n_HTA_split.json, 249 ops) is the QNN/TFLite route; the artifacts the tiles name were sliced from the ONNX route (yolov8n.onnx, 233 nodes -> backbone 103 + head 138 = 241, the slicer materialising the 8 Split ops at the cut). Same network, three op counts, and the tile *boundary* is what agrees across them: group 0 ends where the backbone ONNX ends, and its three outputs are the head's three inputs. Op-level correspondence would need runtime/build_qnn_to_onnx_namemap.py; tile-level is what the runtime dispatches on.
